answer: Trust-transitivity cap with path-disjointness resists sybils: trust between two parties counts only through vertex-DISJOINT honest paths, and each additional unit of trust requires another independent path. A dune of fakes behind a single honest voucher shares that one path — no amount of internal edges manufactures a second disjoint route to the honest core. A garden of genuine agents accumulates trust through many independent paths; a falcon-isolated sybil cluster is capped at the number of truly disjoint honest connections it has, which for a bulk farm behind few vouchers is near one.
